question: How long do we have to close an NCR?
reply:
Close each NCR within 30 calendar days of detection, or record the reason for the extension in the NCR [QMS-003 v1.0 §7.1.2]. Quality Assurance does the closing [QMS-003 v1.0 §7.1.2; QMS-003 v1.0 §3].

Closure requires that the disposition is complete, the final status is set and any CAPA number is linked [QMS-003 v1.0 §6.7.2].

question: What is the analytical flow rate and the total run time of the LC method?
reply:
The analytical flow is 5 µL/min (two nano pumps combined), through the trap column onto the analytical column [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2]. The total run time is 8 min, starting at injection (time zero). This does not include the time the autosampler needs to draw the sample [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2].

If the method file TM-104-M02 differs from this table, do not acquire. Follow TM-104 §8.3 [TM-104 v1.0 §7.2].

question: What signal-to-noise ratio must the heavy (SIS) peak of a sample well reach, and what happens if it does not?
reply:
The heavy (SIS) peak of a sample well must have S/N > 5. Otherwise the result is invalid [TM-105 v2.0 §8.2].

- The Associate Scientist marks that protein result of the sample "invalid – SIS failure" [TM-105 v2.0 §7.3.4].
- For each result marked "invalid – SIS failure", the Associate Scientist follows TM-105 §8.3 as a sample-level nonconformity [TM-105 v2.0 §7.3.5].

The excerpts do not include TM-105 §8.3, so the steps of that nonconformity handling are not covered here.

question: The system suitability test failed. What do I do?
reply:
If any SST criterion fails:

1. Do not inject samples, and keep the plate at 4 °C in the autosampler. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.6]
2. Raise an NCR (QMS-003-F01) under QMS-003 §6.1. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.7]
3. Troubleshoot only through actions recorded in the NCR, e.g. leak check, spray check, trap or column replacement. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.8]
4. After a trap or analytical column replacement, MS source cleaning or MS maintenance, establish new SST reference values (TM-104 §7.5.12 to §7.5.15). [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.9]
5. Repeat the SST steps 7.5.1 to 7.5.4: blank, 3 SST injections, evaluation and recording, then Technical Reviewer sign-off. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.10]

The Technical Reviewer signs off the SST record as passed or failed. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.4] The sequence starts only when all criteria pass. [TM-104 v1.0 §7.5.5]

Not covered by the effective SOPs: the content of QMS-003 §6.1 (how the NCR is processed), and the SST reference values in TM-104 §7.5.12 to §7.5.15 and the criteria in TM-104 §8.2. Those sections are not in the excerpts provided.

question: A batch analysis started under TM-105 v1.0 was not finished when v2.0 became effective. Can I finish it under v1.0?
reply:
No. Each batch is analysed under one TM-105 version from start to end [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4]. A batch whose analysis under v1.0 is not complete on the effective date of v2.0 must be analysed again from TM-105 §7.1.1 under v2.0, because v1.0 is then Superseded [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.1; QMS-001 §7.1.1].

- Rework starts again from the raw data files, in a new Skyline document created from TM-105-T01. The stored v1.0 Skyline document is not opened in the new Skyline version or saved again [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.2].
- Training on v1.0 does not qualify an Associate Scientist or Technical Reviewer for v2.0. Training on v2.0 must be recorded before first use [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.3].

question: Where do I record a manual peak integration in Skyline?
reply:
Record each manual integration in the Skyline audit log. The Associate Scientist enters the permitted condition from the manual integration table as the reason, and the reason is mandatory [TM-105 v2.0 §7.2.6].

- Audit logging must be on for the whole life of the batch Skyline document [TM-105 v2.0 §7.2].
- The audit log Detailed Info report is kept as a batch record [TM-105 v2.0 §8.4].

question: Can we still analyse a batch with Skyline 3.6?
reply:
Partly. The excerpts never name Skyline 3.6, so they do not say which Skyline version TM-105 v2.0 requires or whether 3.6 is allowed.

- TM-105 v1.0 and v2.0 use different Skyline versions, and each batch is analysed under one TM-105 version from start to end [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4].
- Once TM-105 v2.0 is effective, v1.0 is Superseded. A batch whose v1.0 analysis is not complete on that date must be analysed again from TM-105 §7.1.1 under v2.0 [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.1].
- Rework of a batch analysed under v1.0 starts from the raw data files in a new Skyline document created from TM-105-T01. The stored v1.0 Skyline document is not opened in the new Skyline version or saved again [TM-105 v2.0 §2.4.2].

Not covered by the effective SOPs: the Skyline version numbers for v1.0 and v2.0, and therefore whether Skyline 3.6 may still be used.
